ceo_round_63_audit_summary.ceo_verdict: Round 63 is better disciplined than Rounds 59-61 because the coder finally chose one concrete adverse event and forced the candidate into an end-to-end loop. The broad candidate is correctly dead. The remaining thread is now much narrower: predict impending clot fragmentation/distal embolization and alter retrieval behavior before the event.
ceo_p0_directives: Execute the two mandatory attacks, but change their purpose: Attack 1 (US20250186070A1) should search for prediction/future/fragment/embolization/break/failure/force trajectory/rate of change/time series/pre-event/warning/anticipate. The question is NOT 'does it say fragmentation?' but 'Does its sensor stream already support prediction of an imminent adverse retrieval event, rather than merely current-state characterization?'

Attack 2 (traction-control prior art): search for traction velocity control, retrieval speed feedback, pull velocity thrombectomy, automated retrieval speed, force-rate control, speed modulation, traction profile optimization. If speed/traction modulation is already disclosed, the actuator disappears from the novelty claim.

Isolate the true primitive: the candidate survives only if sensor stream → new predictive variable → predicts fragmentation before occurrence → specific intervention → measurable reduction in distal embolization, and that entire loop is absent from the prior-art capability landscape.

Pre-register kill conditions: (1) no reliable pre-event signature exists; (2) prediction lead time too short to intervene; (3) existing force/clot-sensing systems already provide equivalent warning; (4) intervention not technically executable in that window; (5) §103 can reconstruct the complete loop.
ceo_round_63_audit_summary.ceo_freeze_statement: Can a measurable intraprocedural signature predict an imminent fragmentation/distal-embolization event early enough to permit an intervention that existing force/impedance/clot-characterization systems cannot execute? That is a legitimate discovery hypothesis. But it is not yet a surviving invention.
ceo_round_63_audit_summary.ceo_pushing_the_envelope_principle: We have now moved past 'Can we sense the clot?' The question is whether the machine can know, seconds before failure, that the clot is about to fragment — and do something technically different in time to stop it.

attack_1_us20250186070a1_fulltext_keywor.verdict: DEFINITIVE NO — US20250186070A1 does NOT teach forward prediction of an imminent adverse event. attack_2_traction_control_prior_art_sear.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE, leaning NOVEL-but-crowded-adjacent. None of 18 reviewed patents teach traction-VELOCITY modulation during thrombectomy based on force feedback. BUT: US11504151B2 (Stryker, cited by CEO) has NOT been full-text swept for velocity/rate/speed/retraction keywords. This is the single largest evidentiary gap.
attack_2_traction_control_prior_art_sear.us11504151b2_assessment: CEO cited US11504151B2 as teaching 'monitoring pull force and adjusting the scraper during retrieval; maintaining pull force in a target range.' Force adjustment and velocity modulation are different actuators — but under CE-012, 'control the pull' is a genus that plausibly covers both force and speed as species. If US11504151B2's claims or description recite pull-rate, withdrawal-rate, or retraction-velocity anywhere, the actuator link collapses to crowded. STATUS: UNKNOWN pending full-text sweep.

ox_alpha_final_assessment.method: Single OX Alpha call (~90s, ~8000 completion tokens) assessing both attacks + true primitive + 5 kill conditions + final verdict.
ox_alpha_final_assessment.section_1_verdict: NO — US20250186070A1 does NOT teach forward prediction. High confidence. Zero prediction keywords + all fragment/failure occurrences are background or current-state. The positive content of the document actively contradicts forward prediction rather than merely omitting it.
ox_alpha_final_assessment.section_2_verdict: INCONCLUSIVE, leaning NOVEL-but-crowded-adjacent. None of 18 reviewed patents teach traction-VELOCITY modulation. BUT US11504151B2 full-text sweep is the single largest evidentiary gap. The distinction between 'modulate aspiration pressure' (taught) and 'modulate traction velocity' (potentially untaught) is partially genuine (different failure physics: aspiration pressure vs strain rate) and partially semantic (both are 'reduce load on clot when danger detected'). Distinction survives only if coupled to friability/strain-rate mechanism.

Attack 2 provisionally established that the traction-velocity actuator (link 4) is NOT taught in thrombectomy, but this is legally fragile pending US11504151B2 sweep. The physics gate (link 3 existence) is the highest-probability kill condition — if no pre-event signature exists, the entire loop collapses regardless of legal status.
